Issued at 1250 PM CDT Tue Oct 20 2026

The region continues to be under a broad upper level ridge, in 
southwest flow, as the cutoff closed low continues to spin off the 
CA coast. At the surface, the region sits between a high to our east 
and frontal boundary to our west. This results in ongoing sfc winds 
to 850mb out of the south/southwest continuing to usher in warmer 
air resulting in warmer than average temps. The ridge flattens a bit 
as a weak shortwave tracks east across Canada with its cold front 
tracking east/southeast across the CWA this evening and a secondary 
weak low developing along the front over western SD and over SD/NE 
by 12Z. By this time the front will be extending from northeastern 
SD through northern NE with the CWA behind the fropa by the late 
morning. With ongoing drier air over the region, no precip is 
expected with the only noticeable feature is winds will be switching 
to the north then northeast behind it as high pressure moves in. 

Behind the shortwave, the ridge amplifies over the region Wednesday 
afternoon and continues over the area through Thursday before 
tracking eastward Friday. Our attention then turns our next system 
as this cutoff low moves onshore over southern CA with split flow as 
a shortwave moves in over western Canada. This low becomes a 
negatively tilted open wave and will track northeastward (and 
northern wave eastward) and somewhat phase together over the 
northern Rockies Friday. This leads to the formation and deepening 
of its surface low with models indicating the center of the low over 
MT Friday morning. However, there is still a bit of a difference in 
exact position and intensity of the low with ENS indicating a 
~1004mb low slightly southward of where GEFS has the low with GEFS 
indicating a bit stronger around ~1000mb. Through Friday evening, 
this low will track eastward then northeastward across ND into 
Canada with ENS still a bit more southeast with the track and GEFS 
more northwest and stronger. By Saturday morning, ENS actually 
accelerates the speed of the low and wave (given weaker setup) as 
GEFS is slower/stronger (and now more southwest of ENS) as its 
positioned either over southwestern or central Manitoba by 12Z 
Thursday where it will continue its track northeast and occluding. 
So still ongoing low confidence in exact position, track, and 
intensity of the low. 

As of now these models show the possibility of showers per warm 
front over NESD/ND/MN Friday as the front lifts northward with NBM 
pops of 25-40% east of the James River. As its cold front tracks 
west to east across the CWA Friday evening through Saturday, precip 
is again possible ahead and along the front. NBM and models not 
really agreeing of QPF coverage just yet, as mentioned, with 
broadbrush pops of 20-35% over central SD. It seems like both NBM 
and models indicate the best chances and better forcing will be 
Friday afternoon/evening (help from diurnal heating) but all depends 
on where the cold front will be. As of now, pops of 20-40% lie east 
of the James Valley Saturday morning/midday and eastern SD into MN 
by afternoon/evening. However amounts overall still look to be light 
with a probability of QPF at or exceeding 0.10" at 15-60% with 
the probability increasing further east in the CWA, highest 
along and east of the Sisseton Hills per mean grand ensemble 
(GEFS/ENS/GEPS) with NBM pretty close to this. At or over a 
0.25" is 20-30% from south central through eastern SD grand
ensemble and up to 40% NBM. Don't be surprised if we get a 
couple thunderstorms associated with a strengthening LLJ, WAA, 
and CAPE within the warm sector Friday! CSU ML guidance does 
indicate a 5% chance of severe over north central and into ND 
and portions of southern SD Friday afternoon.

With pressure gradients steepening ahead of the low and the 850mb 
LLJ ahead of it strengthening to 20-30kts Thursday and 30-50kts 
Friday. Shallow diurnal mixing will lead to gusty surface winds with 
gusts of 20-35mph, highest along and west of the Mo River Thursday 
afternoon with widespread wind gusts by Friday afternoon 30-45mph. 
Probability of wind gusts>45 mph is 30-50% over the southern James 
Valley and far south central SD Friday afternoon. With ongoing WAA 
continued the trend of blending NBM90th for temps through Thursday. 
With Collab kept temps near NBM per low confidence and dealing with 
more clouds with the system. This results in highs overall in the 
upper 60s and 70s for Wednesday and 70s to potentially 80s degrees 
for the end of the week. Probability of temps at 80 or above is 40-
80% Thursday afternoon and 40-90% over central SD highest confidence 
across south central SD. EC EFI values of 0.8 to 0.99 with a shift 
of tails of zero is highlighted for Friday meaning a significant 
amount of EC members have shifted away from the reforecast 
climatology meaning higher confidence on this occurring. NDFD 
records does indicate we could be flirting with record
